originality.rationale: Inspected original manuscript arXiv:2602.17253v1 and identified no canonical Euclidean inball computation for polygon triangulations or sharp comparison across triangulations. The tree all-walk theorem arXiv:1002.2768v1 is an acknowledged and necessary prior ingredient, not a new theorem here. Targeted published research-record and general literature searches disclosed no matching radius and equality theorem. The closest path symmetric-edge-polytope radius result has a distinct diagonal-2 incidence Gram matrix and does not imply this diagonal-3 geometry. Historical priority remains provisional, especially for alternate terminology.
residual_risks: The all-walk path extremal inequality is previously established; novelty is the Euclidean geometric interpretation, its exact inradius and incenter analysis, and sharp triangulation comparison.
An unindexed geometry or spectral-graph treatment might state equivalent radius or optimization formulas under other terminology.

value.rationale: Different triangulations have combinatorially identical crosspolytope homology models and common outer radius sqrt3, yet different intrinsic inradii. The all-dimensional sharp maximum with strict dual-tree optimizer supplies a meaningful geometric extremum, explicit radical value, and full high-dimensional center locus, illuminating metric structure invisible to known face/lattice classifications. The n=4 path/star example makes the distinction concrete; this is more than recomputation of a table or renaming the known tree walk theorem.
